Name: Donkey
Desc: The most common and affordable pack animal. Hardy and fuel-efficient, but slow and not exceptionally strong. The workhorse of the common person.

Name: Pony
Desc: A small, hardy horse breed adapted to rough terrain or vast steppes. Valued for its incredible endurance and efficiency over long distances.

Name: Mule
Desc: A sterile hybrid of a donkey and horse. Prized for its strength, stamina, and intelligence. Can handle terrain and work longer than a horse, making it a premier pack animal.

Name: Riding Horse
Desc: Bred for speed and agility, this horse is ideal for riders, messengers, and lightly packed scouts. Less efficient for heavy loads than a mule.

Name: Tamed Onager
Desc: A wild ass from the deserts of Persia. Faster than a donkey but notoriously difficult to tame and control. A prestigious, if impractical, chariot animal.

Name: Draft Horse
Desc: A heavier, stronger breed of horse, used for pulling wagons and plows. Faster than an ox but requires more care and better quality food (grain).

Name: Heavy Warhorse
Desc: A massive, powerful horse bred to carry a fully armored rider (a cataphract or knight) into battle. Slow to accelerate but devastating in a charge.

Name: Ox
Desc: A castrated bull, the primary beast of burden for heavy pulling. Incredibly strong and steady, but very slow. Can subsist on poor-quality fodder.

Name: Zebu
Desc: A type of domestic cattle from India with a distinctive fatty hump. Highly resistant to heat and drought, making it an ideal draft animal for the region.

Name: Water Buffalo
Desc: A powerful bovine, perfectly adapted for pulling plows and carts through deep mud and water. Slower and less heat-tolerant than an ox on dry land.

Name: Dromedary Camel
Desc: The one-humped 'ship of the desert'. Unmatched endurance in hot, arid climates due to its ability to conserve water. The backbone of caravan trade in Africa and Arabia.

Name: Bactrian Camel
Desc: The two-humped camel of Central Asia. Even stronger than a dromedary and better adapted to cold climates, making it vital for the high-altitude sections of the Silk Road.

Name: Yak
Desc: The primary beast of burden in the high plateaus of the Himalayas. Uniquely adapted to extreme cold and low oxygen environments where other animals would perish.

Name: Reindeer
Desc: A semi-domesticated deer of the far north. A vital resource for northern cultures, used as a pack animal or for pulling sleds over snow and tundra.

Name: Asian Elephant
Desc: A living engine of war and labor. Capable of carrying and pulling immense loads and inspiring terror on the battlefield. Extremely expensive to acquire and maintain.
